concepts.gloss_en: cutting off the seed of Amalek — one of the three commandments upon entering the Land (appears both as verbal noun and as infinitive of purpose)

reason_for_human: Both occurrences cite the identical mitzvah — 'cutting off the seed of Amalek,' one of the three commandments upon entering the Land — the only difference being grammatical form (verbal noun כריתות in LM 35 vs. infinitive להכרית in LM 6), which is inflectional variation of the same lexical concept, not a homograph. The differing symbolic identifications (incense-sparks vs. Yehoshua) are contextual applications of the same act, not different meanings, so I merged the round-1 split into one concept. Kept the noun form as canonical since it names the commandment as a thing.
